review.title: Receiving now applies a bill's carried variance to whatever stock is left after the delivery, with no 5060 split, so stock that was below zero ends up with a wildly wrong unit cost, or 1210 drifts away from the stock valuation
review.scenario: Repro: scratch test rv/rb3neg.test.ts on servd_test_ip2_b_rv. It passes and prints the figures below. Setup: company A, beef at 1,000/kg (100,000 paisa) with currentStock -9 because recipe sales ran ahead of the delivery, which is typical on a go-live day with no opening count. PO for 10 kg at 1,000. Supplier bill for 10 kg at 1,200 is booked BEFORE the goods, so the whole 2,000 variance is carried in 1210. Then receiveGoods brings in 10 kg. The new hook calls applyCarriedBillVarianceTx, whose revalueItem spreads the full 200,000 paisa over onHand = max(0, -9 + 10) = 1 kg, and unitCostCents becomes 300,000 (3,000/kg against a billed price of 1,200). Do the same with the goods received first and the bill second: postSupplierBill puts 9/10 of the variance to 5060 and the cost becomes 120,000. So the item's cost, recipe costing and the COGS of the next sale depend on whether the bill or the goods arrived first. With stock at -15 and the bill first, the receipt leaves stock at -5, revalueItem moves nothing (absorbedCents 0), and the applied audit row still uses up all 10 kg. The 200,000 paisa stays in 1210 with no stock behind it and no 5060 entry, so 1210 ≠ Σ stock × cost permanently until the bill is voided. Goods first for the same case books the 200,000 to 5060. The function existed before, but until this change it had no production caller. BK2's receiving.ts hook is what puts it on every PO receipt.
review.fix: In applyCarriedBillVarianceTx, do the same split that postSupplierBill does at posting time. Revalue only the share still on hand: absorb targetCents × min(onHand, qty) / qty, clamping to the stock that was there before the receipt plus qty. Post the rest, and the rounding gap targetCents − absorbedCents, as Dr/Cr 5060 against 1210 in the bill's company. Do this in the same transaction (postJournalEntry with tx), dated the receipt, and decide what happens under PERIOD_LOCKED: either refuse the receipt or flag posting_failed. Record usedCents on the applied audit row so postSupplierBillVoid's true-up stays exact. This change belongs in supplierPosting.ts, which BK2 does not own. Also add a test for 'bill first, stock below zero'.

review.title: Carried variances on bills posted before this release are never applied for goods already received, and are only partly applied for later receipts
review.scenario: Before BK2, applyCarriedBillVarianceTx had no production caller (only the resimBooks test bridge). Take a live bill booked before its goods (carriedQty 10, carriedCents C), with 4 kg received before this deploy and nothing applied. The next receipt of 6 kg after the deploy starts with doneQty = 0, because no applied rows exist for the earlier 4 kg. It applies 6/10 of C, and the other 4/10 of C stays in 1210 with no stock behind it. A line that was fully received before the deploy keeps all of C in 1210 for good. Nothing is ever applied twice: the effect is under-application and 1210 drift.
review.fix: Add a one-off catch-up, as a reconciliation action or script, owned by the books stream. For each live bill with a 'supplier.bill.variance' record whose carriedQty is above the applied quantity, take the quantity received after the bill was recorded (goods_receipt_lines on that PO line after recordedAt). Apply the missing slices with receiptId set to the old receipt, or expense them to 5060 when the stock is gone. Add it to prodNotes alongside 'ship item 12 with RB-3'.

fix.summary:
Checked all three findings. Each is real. RV-1 and RV-2 need changes in backend/src/modules/accounting/supplierPosting.ts, which this stream does not own. I wrote that change, tested it, and saved it as a patch: /home/user/servd/.handoff/fixes/BK2-RV-supplierPosting.patch (a copy is in my scratchpad). `git apply --check` passes against the current tree. The patch makes three changes:
(1) applyCarriedBillVarianceTx now splits the carried variance at the receipt the same way postSupplierBill does at posting. Of each slice, only the share still on hand is revalued; that share is min(stock after the receipt, quantity received) / quantity received. The rest of the slice, plus the rounding gap, is posted Dr/Cr 5060 against 1210 in the bill's company, inside the same transaction. The entry's sourceType is 'supplier.bill.variance.receipt' and its sourceId is the applied audit row id. The applied audit row now also records usedCents. If the period is closed, the receipt is refused with PERIOD_LOCKED, the same as a bill.
(2) postSupplierBillVoid adds Σ applied usedCents to its true-up, so a void also gives back the 5060 share that receipts expensed.
(3) New applyMissedCarriedBillVariances({ tenantIds, dryRun }) is the one-off catch-up for RV-2. It runs one company at a time and one PO line per transaction. For each PO line it applies min(received quantity no live bill has matched yet, carried quantity not yet applied). The share still on hand is stock now less what the item received after the line's last receipt; the rest goes to 5060. Running it twice changes nothing the second time. It also adds an optional onHandQty input to applyCarriedBillVarianceTx.
In my own files: receiving.ts comments now describe the split and the closed-period refusal. receiving.ts now also writes GoodsReceiptLine.poLineId. That column was added in migration 20260927 but receiveGoods never filled it.
Test file backend/tests/integrationPass2Books.test.ts has 5 new tests in their own company C. They cover:
- stock -9 with the bill first: cost 120,000 and 180,000 to 5060, the same as goods first
- stock -15: 200,000 to 5060, and a void leaves 1210 and 5060 at zero
- stock at or above zero: no change and no 5060 entry
- the RV-2 catch-up: a partly received line ends at 120,000; goods already sold go to 5060; a dry run changes nothing; a second run does nothing; company B's run touches nothing
- a closed period refuses the receipt and nothing moves.
RV-3 is only a comment in orders/service.ts, which is not my file.

review.title: The manager who raised a PO is still offered Receive, the PO is preselected, and every Accept is refused with 403 and logs a high-severity exception flag
review.scenario: Owner decision 27 says whoever raised a PO cannot receive it; only the CEO is exempt. Take a boh_management or fnb_manager user who raises a PO. On /procurement, PoActions shows them 'Receive' because canReceive only checks MANAGERS. On /procurement/receiving?poId=…, the PO loads into the form. When they press 'Accept delivery', POST /crosschecks/receiving calls assertNotSelfApproval and returns 403 SELF_APPROVAL_BLOCKED. It also writes a high-severity 'self_approval' ExceptionFlag ('Self-approval blocked: receive goods'). This is confirmed by backend/tests/receiving.test.ts:137-138, which I ran green on servd_test_ip2_f_rv. So an honest click shows the user a red error and puts a high-severity alert in the CEO's exceptions inbox. The builder sent this to the owner as a question and said the fix 'needs the PO's createdBy in the purchase-orders list response'. That premise is wrong. GET /procurement/purchase-orders (procurement/routes.ts:303, `include` returns all scalars) and GET /crosschecks/receiving/open-pos (crosschecks/routes.ts:73) both already return `createdBy`. The receiving page's pos array already has it.
review.fix: Add `createdBy?: string | null` to the OpenPo and PurchaseOrder types. Make it so the user can receive only if they are a manager and either their role is 'admin' or `po.createdBy !== user.id`. Use that rule in PoActions (show 'View at dock' or a short 'You raised this, a colleague receives it' instead of Receive) and in the receiving page (skip the ?poId= preselect for the PO's creator, and disable or mark that PO in the Step 1 picker). Use the store's user.id. No backend change is needed, and decision 27 already covers the owner question.

review.title: The read-only dock view says 'No purchase orders waiting' when its reads were actually refused
review.scenario: canOpenPath lets any role holding the 'procurement' module open /procurement/receiving, and the CEO can grant that module to, say, finance. The page's reads (/crosschecks/receiving, /receiving/open-pos, /receiving/suppliers) only accept PROCUREMENT_TEAM, which is MANAGERS plus procurement. For such a user every query returns 403, `pos` falls back to `[]`, and the new read-only section shows 'No purchase orders waiting to be received.' with 'Recent deliveries · 0'. The user is told the dock is empty when they were in fact refused. The procurement page sends exactly these non-managers here through the new 'View at dock' button.
review.fix: Read `error` from the open-pos and receipts queries. When either fails, show its message (for example in the existing ErrorBanner style) instead of the empty-state text.

fix.summary:
I confirmed both findings and fixed both. A test that checks the backend behaviour these pages rely on passes. The existing receiving suite passes 10/10, and the admin typecheck is clean.

FE2-RV-01 was real. The backend blocks whoever raised a PO from receiving it, unless their role is `admin`. Each blocked attempt returns 403 `SELF_APPROVAL_BLOCKED` and logs a high-severity `self_approval` exception flag. Both `GET /procurement/purchase-orders` and `GET /crosschecks/receiving/open-pos` already return `createdBy`, so no backend change was needed.
- **/procurement:** `PurchaseOrder` now has `createdBy`, and both pages check it with a new `raisedByMe(po, user)` helper. A manager who raised the PO now sees "View at dock" instead of "Receive". The button's tooltip says "You raised this PO, so a colleague receives it". Non-managers get the tooltip "A manager takes the delivery in".
- **/procurement/receiving:** `OpenPo` now has `createdBy`. Opening `?poId=` no longer preselects the PO when it is the user's own, and a note says "You raised PO X, so a colleague receives it." In the Step 1 picker, the user's own POs are disabled and labelled "You raised this, a colleague receives it", so they can never reach "Accept delivery" and trigger the 403 and the flag. The CEO, and POs with no creator on file, can still be received, as on the server.

FE2-RV-02 was real. The dock reads only admit `PROCUREMENT_TEAM`, so a role such as finance that was given the procurement module gets 403 on them. The page now reads `error` from the open-POs and recent-deliveries queries and shows each failure in a red banner with the server's message. When a read fails it no longer says "No purchase orders waiting to be received." or shows "Recent deliveries · 0". This applies to both the read-only view and the manager view. `ErrorBanner` now takes a `label`, and the save error keeps "Save failed:".

Nothing was rejected. I only edited the two procurement pages. The other files listed under my stream (period-close, the reconciliation page, `appRoles.ts` and the workforce page) were not part of these two findings, so I left them alone.

items.note: Confirmed against backend/src/lib/separation-of-duties.ts (only role admin is exempt; blocked attempts raise a high-severity flag). Both PO list endpoints already return createdBy. Added createdBy to the PurchaseOrder and OpenPo types and a raisedByMe() check in both pages. /procurement: the PO's raiser sees 'View at dock' with a tooltip instead of 'Receive'. /procurement/receiving: ?poId= is not preselected for the raiser and a note is shown instead; the raiser's own POs are disabled and labelled in the Step 1 picker. CEO and POs with no creator on file can still be received, as on the server.

Confirmed: open-pos and GET /crosschecks/receiving are PROCUREMENT_TEAM only (a finance user gets 403, checked in the scratch test). The receiving page now reads both query errors and shows a red banner with the server message. When a read fails it hides the 'No purchase orders waiting' text and the 'Recent deliveries · 0' count. This applies to the read-only and manager views. ErrorBanner now takes a label.

fix.tests: The admin frontend has no unit-test setup, so the UI change itself is not tested. Instead I added a backend test that checks the server behaviour the UI depends on, and ran it against a new test DB, servd_test_fe2_dock (dropped afterwards), with Redis on 6390/25: 2/2 pass. The test lives in the scratchpad at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-servd/33ef43a5-b49c-56f9-95d2-440e3a7d20b8/scratchpad/fe2/dockContract.test.ts (it runs with the vitest.config.ts next to it), not in the repo. It checks that both PO lists return createdBy, that company B cannot see company A's PO, that the PO's raiser gets 403 SELF_APPROVAL_BLOCKED while another manager (fnb_manager) receives it with 201, and that finance gets 403 with a message on both dock reads. The existing backend/tests/receiving.test.ts passes 10/10 on the same DB. `npx tsc --noEmit -p frontend/admin` passes.
fix.needsOtherFiles: Optional: the scratchpad test fe2/dockContract.test.ts could be copied into the repo as backend/tests/receivingDockContract.test.ts (or merged into backend/tests/receiving.test.ts) so that a future change cannot drop createdBy from the PO lists without a test failing. I don't own those files, so I didn't add it.
fix.prodNotes: Frontend only, no backend or schema change. The pages hide or disable Receive using the same rule the server applies, so the server stays the authority.
